note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A). Every assert is derived by hand from the 6-wire topology and the printed rule (p.24 step 5: changing switch 6 reverses the motor), not from printed dial positions; the page prints no direction. Topology: 6R and 6W on 6+, 6T and 6U on 6- (6-/6T, 6T/6U); arm 6S feeds D18 and arm 6V feeds D17. Switch LEFT (rest, nc): D18 +, D17 -. Switch RIGHT (no): D18 -, D17 +. The absolute sense (D17 + / D18 - toward increasing numbers) is the O-R11 ruling, [likely], not printed on this page. The reversal is encoded without a direction observable (O-C14) by pad-by-pad until steps: each one-pitch leg has maxMs 400 and each reversal leg maxMs 600, both well under the 15 pitches the wiper would need going the long way round, so a dial that kept its direction, or ran the other sense, fails. The window rests on the run rate (O-R3, 45 rpm fallback): the legs pass from about 13 rpm and stay decisive up to about 85 rpm. The reversal legs tolerate any coast during the slide's break-before-make stroke (O-R5) up to about one pitch. Start position D0 is the construction default, not printed. Rotary geometry, run rate and coast remain profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3 and O-R5.
